summary: IPTV Live TV merge verified end-to-end. 15/15 backend pytest cases pass (backend/tests/test_iptv_livetv.py) covering channel-list merge, stream URL minting, HLS manifest rewrite, encrypted segment pass-through, IPTV metadata, logo proxy, and Plex regression. Frontend at /watch/live shows source chips 'All (5,382)' and 'IPTV (5,382)', live-search filters correctly (gibberish -> empty state), 300 IPTV cards render with LIVE badge + logos, clicking a card navigates to /watch/play/iptv-live-<id> and triggers the full network pipeline (livetv/channels -> metadata/iptv-live -> stream/iptv-live -> iptv/p/live/*.m3u8 -> iptv/pass — all HTTP 200). Plex is not connected in this preview DB, so plex chip is absent (expected per E1 note). No functional bugs found.

minor.issue: Backend correctly sets 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable' but the ingress/CF layer rewrites it to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' before it reaches the client. Not a backend bug per se, but logos will be re-fetched every session because of it. Content-Type is preserved (image/png).

issues: Search field caps display at 300 (MAX_SHOW). When typing a broad term like 'espn' the count stays at 300, which is correct given 5k+ channels, but there is no 'x more matches — refine search' hint until the user scrolls to the very bottom. Consider surfacing the overflow indicator above the grid when a search is active.

In headless Chromium the HLS.js player throws 'Playback error (bufferAddCodecError)' — expected/acceptable per E1 note (headless codec support). All network fetches (manifest + first segment) return 200. On real browsers/Fire TV this should render correctly assuming the stream codecs are supported.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Consider adding overflow banner (e.g. 'Showing 300 of N matches') at the top of the live-grid when search is active, so users know they may still need to refine.
OPTIONAL: If browsers should cache proxied logos, work around the ingress/CF Cache-Control rewrite (currently everything becomes no-store).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1945 lines — well past the 700-line threshold. Strongly consider extracting the IPTV subsystem (config, proxy, passthrough, logo, stream URL minting, m3u8 rewrite) into a separate module (e.g. backend/iptv.py) mounted on the same APIRouter. Same for Plex logic.

_rewrite_m3u8 always base64-Fernet-encrypts the full absolute URL for every segment on every request. For a long/live playlist this is CPU-noticeable; consider caching the manifest for a few seconds (Xtream typically increments segment names, so the same URL is only rewritten once per rotation anyway).

The passthrough endpoint always requires ?t=<user-jwt>, but Fernet ciphertext k already binds the URL — the token+ciphertext double-check is fine, but token expiry (6h) is the only revocation. That is acceptable for now.

iptv_proxy uses `ext` freely in the URL join; validated 'kind' is in {live,movie,series} but no explicit whitelist on `ext`. Not exploitable (fernet is separate), but a whitelist ('m3u8', 'ts', 'mp4') would harden it.

live_channels returns Plex channels first then merges IPTV — with 5k IPTV channels the response payload is ~700KB+. Frontend already caps display at 300, but the API itself has no pagination/limit param. Consider ?q=&limit= server-side to reduce initial load.

iptv_logo endpoint is public (no auth) with `u=` accepting any http/https URL — effectively an open image proxy. Low-risk since payload is passed through untouched and content-type is whatever upstream serves, but it could be abused to obscure the source IP for HTTP GETs. Consider (a) restricting host to the configured IPTV domain, or (b) rate-limiting.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (chips, search, filter, empty state, card click → /watch/play/iptv-live-*, full manifest+segment network pipeline all verified)
